4_D11_pin.a2_check: a2 (minimal real scalar, xi=0) = (1/180)(Riem^2 - Ric^2) + (1/2)(1/6)^2 R^2 = C^2/120 - E/360 + R^2/72 (verified by coefficient matching); with C^2 -> 1/2 P2 and R^2 -> 3 P0s: 1/240 : 1/24 = 1:10 = own c2:c0
4_D11_pin.absolute_pin_assessment: derivable from package data, at least in magnitude: (i) N_eps = i S_eps/(16 pi^2) (integrals.py), G = kappa^2 N_eps Ghat MB, so c2 N_eps = (-i/240)(i/16pi^2) = 1/(240*16pi^2), real, i.e. the observed common factor -i is exactly cancelled by N_eps; (ii) heat-kernel side: |W_div| = (1/(32 pi^2 eps)) int a2; second h-derivative of (1/120) C^2 with C^2 -> (kappa^2/2) p^4 h P2 h gives kappa^2/(240*16 pi^2 eps) -- same magnitude; (iii) the remaining overall sign (G vs Gamma^(2), Minkowski i in the Feynman rules, sign of W_div) must be fixed from the package's declared G6/amplitude convention -- the one piece not derived. In addition M2 (P18) already matched the D11 L-coefficient absolutely against the inherited XVI-O kernel (c_FT = i pi^2), and L-coefficient = -pole for D11, so an overall x2 is caught by M2 today. Recommendation: derive the pin as c_k * N_eps vs (1/2)(1/16pi^2) a2 coefficients with the declared sign convention, rather than leaving it OPEN.
